prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's relaxed density-weight floor (0.5*LOWER_PCOF) helps wirelength/timing but the *asymmetric* band still lets density pressure ramp up aggressively in early iterations before HPWL signal is meaningful; making the density weight growth slower during the first iterations (when overflow is still high and HPWL noisy) and letting it relax fully later will reduce residual congestion-driven detours that hurt TNS, without starving density control at the end.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.487 robust(mean-std)=+0.138 min_case=+0.131 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.131 dWNS=+6.3% dTNS=+18.1% overflow~108
  bp-ng45: score=+0.191 dWNS=+11.9% dTNS=+24.3% overflow~80
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.165 dWNS=+13.4% dTNS=+18.6% overflow~105
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains (+18–24%) exceeding dWNS (+6–13%), consistent with reduced congestion-driven detours rather than raw timing push. Overflow (~80–108) stayed controlled, so density wasn't starved. The slower early density-weight ramp plausibly let HPWL signal mature before density pressure dominated, cutting residual detours that hurt TNS. Next step: sweep the early-iteration growth rate (e.g., 2–3 slower schedules) to find where TNS gain saturates before overflow regresses, and verify on a larger case set.
